newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street executive nominated for Treasury post.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street executive nominated for Treasury post.

text.p: The White House on Friday named a top Goldman Sachs financier on Friday as its nominee to take over the vacant post of Assistant Treasury Secretary for Financial Markets.

The Treasury Department announced that Gary Gensler, a partner in the Wall Street firm in which Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin formerly was a senior executive, was nominated for the job that includes overseeing the sale of U.S. Treausry securities to finance the government's debt.
The post has been vacant since February, when Jeffrey Shafer resigned it.
Gensler joined the international investment banking firm, The Goldman Sachs Group L.P., in 1979 and since 1995 has been its co-head of finance for worldwide operations.
At the same time, Treasury announced that Assistant Treasury Secretary David Lipton has been nominated for promotion to Under Secretary of the Treasury for International Affairs.

Lipton, who joined Treasury in 1993, has had a broad role in coordinating international and economic policy with industrialized and poorer nations and developing policy toward multilateral bodies like the International Monetary Fund.
Rubin praised Lipton's contribution to fulfilling Treasury's international economic role.
"He has been a key contributor to our policy toward Russia and the Ukraine and has been instrumental in shaping the economic and financial aspects of our policy in Bosnia," Rubin said in a statement.

In addition, Treasury said that Nancy Killefer was nominated to be Assistant Treasury Secretary for Management and Chief Financial Officer. The job includes reposnsibility for Treasury's budget and for personnel policy.
Killefer is a director of management consulting firm McKinsey & Co Inc.
